\begin{chapstatus}{Roadmap of this chapter}
By the end of the chapter you can:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item explain how a MOS transistor works as a switch and how CMOS builds a gate
\item read logic levels and noise margins from voltages
\item size the resistor of an LED and explain the pull-up of a button
\end{enumerate}
It builds on: only the setup of Chapter~\ref{ch:setup}. Next: Chapter~\ref{ch:combinational}.
\par\smallskip\textbf{Looking back, looking ahead.} In Lecture 02 the counter survived from one frame to the next in memory, not in a register. Today a memory cell costs about 6 transistors and a flip-flop about 20: remembering a bit is a circuit. Lecture 13 shows how latches and flip-flops keep a bit. \emph{Recall:} Where did the counter of Lecture 02 live between two frames, and why not in t1?
\end{chapstatus}
